context_from_centrix: property.heating_type and heating_central (central gas boiler with hot water tank in the demo building)
open cases in the same building (neighbour already reported?)
building notices (planned maintenance / water shut-off today)

safety_first.question: Before anything else: do you smell gas anywhere near the boiler or kitchen?

if_yes.tenant_message: Please leave the apartment now, don't use light switches or open flames, and call the gas emergency line 0800 2 26 77 89 from outside. I've alerted your property manager right away.

questions.text: Is it only the shower, or is the hot water cold at the sinks too?

answers.only_shower: only the shower is cold, sinks are hot

questions.text: Are the radiators cold as well?
Did someone else shower or use a lot of hot water just before you?

answers.yes: others used hot water just before

questions.text: Did you let the hot water run for one or two minutes?
Could you send a photo of the boiler's display? It usually shows an error code if something's wrong.

answers.code: display shows an error code (read from photo)

questions.text: Are the lights and other electrics working in your apartment?
If you have a gas stove: does it light normally?
Could you check the shower's temperature knob: is it turned fully to warm, and is there a safety button at 38°C you need to press to go hotter?

answers.was_wrong: knob was set too cold / limiter

questions.text: On the boiler there's a small pressure gauge. Is the needle below 1 bar?
Does the water eventually get warm if you wait longer, or does it stay cold?

answers.slow: gets lukewarm after a long wait

questions.text: Is it just this one tap, with very weak flow, maybe on an outside wall?

answers.yes: one tap, weak flow, outside wall

causes.label: Hot water tank used up (others showered just before)
causes.tenant_message: That's probably just the hot water tank being empty after the others showered. It reheats in about 30–45 minutes. I'll check back with you in an hour, and if it's still cold I'll send someone.

causes.label: Hot water not run long enough (long pipe to the shower)
causes.tenant_message: In older buildings the hot water takes a moment to reach the shower. Could you let it run for about two minutes and tell me if it gets warm?

causes.label: Shower thermostat set too cold or scald limiter engaged
causes.tenant_message: Most shower thermostats stop at 38°C: press the small button on the knob and turn further to go hotter. Let me know if that does it!

causes.label: Shower mixer / thermostatic cartridge faulty
causes.tenant_message: Since the sinks are hot and only the shower stays cold, it's most likely the shower's mixer cartridge. That's a quick job for a plumber. I'll arrange one for you.

causes.label: Boiler fault (e.g. F.28 ignition failed)
causes.tenant_message: The boiler reports a fault, so it's not something you can fix yourself. I'll get a certified heating technician out to you.

causes.label: Heating water pressure too low (F.22)
causes.tenant_message: The system pressure is a bit low. Our caretaker can top it up in a few minutes, so no technician needed for now. I'll let them know.

causes.label: Hot water circulation pump faulty
causes.tenant_message: If the water only gets lukewarm after a long wait everywhere, the hot water circulation pump is probably failing. I'll send a heating technician to check it.

causes.label: Hot water tank thermostat or scale build-up
causes.tenant_message: The heating works but the hot water doesn't, so it's likely the hot water tank's thermostat or limescale. I'll arrange a heating technician.

causes.label: Boiler has no power (tripped fuse / outage)
causes.escalate_if: fuse trips again or caretaker can't restore power
causes.tenant_message: The boiler seems to have no power. Our caretaker will check the fuse box first. If that's not it, I'll send an electrician.

causes.label: Gas supply interrupted
causes.tenant_message: It looks like the gas supply itself is interrupted. Your property manager is contacting the gas supplier now. I'll keep you posted.

causes.label: Planned maintenance / water shut-off (known in centrix)
causes.tenant_message: There's planned maintenance in your building today; hot water should be back by the time in the notice. Sorry for the hassle!

causes.label: Frozen or damaged pipe
causes.tenant_message: Weak flow at just one tap on an outside wall sounds like a frozen or damaged pipe. Please don't try to heat it with an open flame. I'm sending a plumber.

strategy: Always run safety_first before anything else.
Use centrix context before asking: a neighbour's open report on the same central boiler means boiler_fault is very likely; a building notice today means planned_maintenance.
Ask the single question that best splits the remaining causes (usually q_scope, then q_radiators or q_recent_use).
Stop as soon as one cause is clearly most likely (≤ 3 questions typical); never ask more than 5.
Self-help outcomes: give the tip, schedule a follow-up check, and do NOT dispatch anyone.
Technician outcomes: pick partners whose trades include the cause's trade (and brand if required), then staff approval.
Always tell the tenant the likely cause in plain words, and record the diagnosis with the reasoning on the case.
